settings.emergencyContactHint: The telephone number the IMDG Code and the IATA DGR require on the declaration.
settings.signatureHint: Draw it once and it is ready on every shipment from then on. It stays replaceable per shipment.
settings.adminIntro: These settings apply to the whole installation.
settings.adminDefaultLanguageHint: The language for anyone who has not chosen one yet.

settings.catalogAutoSyncHint: Refreshes goods and profile data when the container starts.
settings.unCardsEnabledHint: The UN card download offered with a shipment carrying dangerous goods.
settings.sessionTimeoutHint: How long someone stays signed in. 480 is one working day.
settings.assistantIntro: The assistant always works; a local model only makes reading free text more flexible.
settings.assistantUnpinned: The sources are not yet pinned by hash in this release; the download stays off until they are.
settings.assistantFootprint: Needs about 2.5 GB RAM and 2 GB disk. The download is verified against a pinned SHA-256.
settings.updateCheckHint: Asks GitHub whether a newer version exists. Off means no request ever leaves.
settings.updateExplain: Updating is always: pull the newer image and recreate the container — from the server, for example:
settings.updateAuto: With Watchtower this happens by itself; on Unraid one click on 'update' in the Docker tab is enough.
settings.unCardsStoreIntro: Cards generated by EMCargo, installed on the data volume — not part of the Docker image.
settings.unCardsNone: No card set is installed yet. Download the latest set, or import a downloaded ZIP file.
settings.unCardsNoRelease: No published card set was found yet.
settings.unCardsRemoteUnreachable: GitHub is unreachable; whether a newer set exists cannot be determined right now.
settings.unCardsImportDone: The card set was validated and installed.
settings.unCardsRemoveConfirm: Remove the local card set? The wizard cannot offer UN cards until a new set is imported.
settings.unCardsRemoved: The local card set was removed.
settings.updateUnreachable: GitHub could not be reached, so whether a newer version exists is unknown.
settings.updateUpToDate: You are running the newest version ({{version}}).
settings.updateApplyHint: Takes one to a few minutes; EMCargo is briefly unavailable and then reloads by itself.
settings.updateApplyConfirm: EMCargo will update to v{{version}} and restart in the process. Running downloads will be cut off. Continue?
settings.updatePhaseRestarting: The application is restarting — this page reloads as soon as the new version answers.
settings.updateDone: Update succeeded: you are now running version {{version}}.
settings.updateFailed: The last update did not succeed: {{error}} The previous version keeps running.
settings.updateTimeout: The new version did not answer within ten minutes. Check the container on the server.
settings.updateEnableApplyHow: Mount the Docker socket, set the environment variable and restart the container once; an update button then appears here:
settings.updateSocketWarning: Careful: mounting the Docker socket effectively gives this container administrator rights over the whole server.
settings.updateReasonNoSocket: The switch is on, but no Docker socket is mounted into the container — add the volume line above and restart the container.
settings.updateReasonSwitchOff: In-app installation is not enabled yet. Add UPDATE_APPLY_ENABLED=true to the container settings and restart it.
settings.updateReasonPermission: The socket is mounted, but the app is not permitted to open it. Fixed since v1.135.0 — update the container manually once more and restart.
settings.updateReasonContainerNotFound: The socket works, but the app cannot find its own container at the Docker daemon.
settings.updateReasonForeignImage: This container does not run the official EMCargo image; in-app updating stays off.
settings.updateReasonSocketUnusable: The Docker socket is mounted but does not respond usably; check the mount and restart the container.
settings.mailHint: How EMCargo sends mail. Without a server the app sends nothing.
settings.mailEnabledHint: Off means no outgoing mail at all, not even a test.
settings.mailHostHint: For example smtp.gmail.com, or the address of your own relay.
settings.mailUsernameHint: Leave empty if the server asks for no sign-in.
settings.mailPasswordHint: Kept on the server and never sent back to the browser.
settings.mailPasswordStored: A password is stored. Leave empty to keep it; type something to replace it.
settings.mailFromHint: Most servers refuse a sender that is not their own.
settings.mailTestHint: Sends a short message using the saved settings.
settings.mailTestSaveFirst: Save first: the test uses the saved settings.
settings.publicUrlHint: Used for the links in outgoing mail, for example https://emcargo.example.com. Leave empty when the browser reaches EMCargo directly.
settings.cardLinks: QR code with UN cards on documents
settings.cardLinksHint: Puts a QR code on every transport document that opens this consignment's UN cards. The page behind it does not ask for a sign-in — deliberately: the driver at the roadside and the responder on the scene have no account here. It shows only the UN numbers and whether a card exists for each; nothing about the consignment, the parties or the quantities. Off unless you turn it on.
settings.cardLinksNeedsUrl: Fill in the public address above first. Without it no QR code is printed: a code on paper that leads nowhere is worse than no code, because whoever holds the paper cannot tell the difference.
settings.twoFactorPolicyHint: Who must use a second step when signing in. Anyone without one is asked to set it up after signing in.
settings.introOpen: Set the app up the way you use it. What you save here stays in this browser and never reaches the server; it goes when you clear your browser data.
settings.myDetailsHintOpen: Details that are the same on nearly every shipment. They stay in this browser.
settings.adminBrandingHint: The installation's own name and pictures: in the header, on the sign-in page and on the tiles. The pictures apply the moment they are uploaded; the name is saved with the button below.
settings.brandNameHint: Shown in the header, on the sign-in page and in the browser tab. Empty means EMCargo.
settings.brandLogoHint: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 1 MB. Shown at its own colours in both themes, and carried in outgoing mail.
settings.brandModalitiesHint: One image per transport mode, PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 3 MB. Use a landscape image with the subject centred; the crop adapts to the screen.
settings.updateNative: This installation runs as its own service on the server, without Docker. Updating is the installation's update script: it fetches the new release, puts it beside the old one and restarts the service. The data stays where it is.
settings.updateKubernetes: This installation runs in Kubernetes. Updating is a rollout to the newer image; the pod is recreated and the volume stays.
settings.auditRetentionHint: How long a line stays in the audit log. Whatever is older is removed at start-up. 365 is one year.
settings.historyEnabledHint: On: the export step keeps every shipment when its documents are downloaded, and the Shipments, Trips and Articles pages, the address book and the safety adviser's annual report appear. Off: nothing is kept, and switching off is only possible once the kept shipments and trips are deleted — this screen asks first.
settings.historyDiscardTitle: Switch the history off and delete what it kept?
settings.historyDiscardBody: The history still holds {{shipments}} kept shipment(s) and {{trips}} kept trip(s). Switching off deletes them for good; the address book, the articles and the annual reports stay. This cannot be undone.

customsRoute.ens_entering: Goods from {{from}} enter the ICS2 area (EU customs territory, Northern Ireland, Norway, Switzerland) in {{to}}: the carrier lodges an entry summary declaration in ICS2. Fill in its MRN once known.
customsRoute.ens_within_area: {{from}} and {{to}} are both inside the ICS2 area: no entry summary declaration for this movement.
customsRoute.ens_leaving: The goods leave the ICS2 area ({{from}} to {{to}}): the entry summary declaration is for goods coming in; the export side has its own declaration (export MRN).
customsRoute.ens_outside: Neither {{from}} nor {{to}} is in the ICS2 area. Only if the goods are brought into it on the way — a stop, not a mere passage through its waters or airspace (Art. 127(2)(a) UCC) — would the carrier lodge an entry summary declaration.
customsRoute.aes_export: Export from {{from}} to {{to}}: Electronic Export Information is filed in AES (15 CFR 30.2). The ITN belongs on the transport document — unless every commodity line is USD 2,500 or less (§ 30.37(a)) or another exemption applies.
customsRoute.aes_puerto_rico: Between the United States and Puerto Rico ({{from}} to {{to}}) Electronic Export Information is filed too (15 CFR 30.2(a)(1)).
customsRoute.aes_virgin_islands: To the U.S. Virgin Islands from {{from}} Electronic Export Information is filed (15 CFR 30.2(a)(1)).
customsRoute.aes_canada: Shipments originating in the United States (the 50 states and the District of Columbia) with Canada as country of ultimate destination are exempt from filing (15 CFR 30.36) — not when the goods are stored in Canada for a third country, move through Canada to a third destination, or need a licence (§ 30.2(a)(1)(iv)).
customsRoute.aes_not_named: From the U.S. Virgin Islands to {{to}} is not among the movements 15 CFR 30.2(a)(1) names.
customsRoute.aes_not_us: The goods do not leave from the United States ({{from}}): no AES filing.
customsRoute.aes_domestic: {{from}} to {{to}} is a domestic movement: no AES filing.
customsRoute.ens_uk_entering: Goods from {{from}} enter Great Britain: HMRC asks the carrier for an entry summary declaration in the Safety and Security GB service, from the EU included. Fill in its reference once known.
customsRoute.ens_uk_qualifying_ni: From Northern Ireland into Great Britain: qualifying Northern Ireland goods have a waiver from the entry summary declaration (HMRC); other goods need one in the Safety and Security GB service.
customsRoute.ens_domestic: {{from}} to {{to}} is a domestic movement: no entry summary declaration.
customsRoute.aes_territory: Goods shipped from the U.S. territories, or between the United States and them ({{from}} to {{to}}), are excluded from filing (15 CFR 30.2(d)(2)); only goods transiting them to a foreign destination are filed.

legal.title: Disclaimer and licence
legal.intro: EMCargo is a tool that prepares transport and accompanying documents based on your input. It does not provide legal, customs or safety advice. Please read the terms below carefully; by using EMCargo you accept them.

sections.heading: 1. Draft — not a final document
sections.body: Every document produced by EMCargo is a draft. Before use, hand-over, submission or signature it must be fully verified, completed and signed by a duly authorised and qualified person. Signature fields, carrier data and operational fields are deliberately not pre-filled.

sections.heading: 2. Dangerous goods
sections.body: Classification, packaging, marking, labelling and documentation of dangerous goods (ADR, RID, ADN, IMDG, IATA DGR) are the exclusive responsibility of the shipper and other legally designated parties. EMCargo never automatically turns a free-text description into a final classification and does not replace certified master data, a safety adviser or the current, authorised regulations.

sections.heading: 3. No warranties (AS IS)
sections.body: The software and all generated documents are provided "AS IS" and "AS AVAILABLE", without any express or implied warranty, including warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, accuracy, timeliness, completeness or non-infringement. No warranty is given that reference data or form templates are correct, current or complete.

sections.heading: 4. Limitation of liability
sections.body: To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, the author(s), rights holder(s) and contributors of EMCargo exclude all liability for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, punitive or consequential damages — including loss of profit, business interruption, fines, penalties, delays, seized or refused shipments, loss of or damage to goods, environmental damage, personal injury or loss of data — arising out of or in connection with the use of, or inability to use, the application or the generated documents, on any legal basis and even if advised of the possibility of such damage. You use EMCargo entirely at your own risk.

sections.heading: 5. Indemnification

carrier.intro: Paste the carrier's confirmation; the recognisable references (AWB number, booking number, ENS MRN, AES ITN) are read and put only into fields that are still empty. Nothing is stored.
carrier.placeholder: Paste the confirmation e-mail text here…

users.title: Users
users.intro: Accounts for this installation. Only administrators see this page.
users.guardSelf: Not possible on your own account — ask another administrator.
users.guardLastAdmin: This is the last active administrator; it cannot be removed or demoted.
users.inviteHint: The new user chooses their own password through a link. The link works for seven days.
users.passwordByInvite: Not needed: the user chooses a password through the invitation.
users.inviteNoMailServer: Account created, but no mail server is configured, so the invitation was not sent.
users.inviteFailed: Account created, but the invitation could not be sent: {{reason}}
users.clearTwoFactorHint: Removes this user's second step, for a lost phone.
users.clearTwoFactorConfirm: Remove two-factor verification for {{name}}? They will sign in with a password alone afterwards.

reset.title: New password
reset.intro: Choose a new password for your account.
reset.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
reset.done: Your password is set. You can sign in now.
reset.noToken: This page belongs to a link from an e-mail. Ask for a new link on the sign-in screen.
reset.spent: This link has already been used or has expired. Ask for a new one on the sign-in screen with 'Forgot your password?'.

twoFactor.title: Two-factor verification
twoFactor.intro: A second step when signing in: a code from an app, or a code by e-mail.
twoFactor.requiredHere: This installation requires two-factor verification for your account. Set it up below.
twoFactor.onByMail: On, with a code by e-mail.
twoFactor.turnOffHint: Type a working code; otherwise a borrowed session is enough to strip the protection.
twoFactor.scan: Scan this code with your authenticator app.
twoFactor.mailSent: We sent a code to your e-mail address.
twoFactor.enterCode: Code from the app or the message
twoFactor.recoveryHint: You see these once. Each works one time, for when your phone is gone. Without them and without your phone you need an administrator.
twoFactor.codeSent: A code has been sent to your e-mail address.
twoFactor.turnOffHintMail: Ask for a code first and type it below. A recovery code works too.
twoFactor.nudge: Protect your account with two-factor verification.
twoFactor.nudgeRequired: Your organisation requires two-factor verification. Set it up to continue.
twoFactor.enforced: Until your account has two-factor verification, this is the only screen that works. Set it up below.
twoFactor.renewHint: Enter a current authenticator, email or recovery code. The new recovery codes replace all previous codes.

cards.title: UN cards
cards.subtitle: Reference cards for {{modality}}
cards.none: No UN numbers in this link.
cards.unavailable: This installation does not share cards by link.
cards.note: This page shows reference material per UN number only. It says nothing about the consignment, the parties or the quantities.

groupage.title: Groupage
groupage.intro: Several consignments on one vehicle, judged together. Three rules apply per transport unit rather than per consignment: the 1.1.3.6 points, the mixed loading of 7.5.2 and the limited-quantities marking of 3.4.13.
groupage.addHint: Choose the JSON exports the export step writes for each consignment — or, on an installation that keeps its shipments, the structured export the shipments page offers per kept shipment.
groupage.unitMass: Permitted maximum mass of the transport unit (tonnes)
groupage.unitMassHint: 3.4.13 applies only above 12 tonnes. This is the one fact about the load the application cannot derive; leave it empty and the limited-quantities marking is reported as undecided rather than guessed.
groupage.needTwo: Add at least two consignments: with one, this check says nothing the consignment did not already say.
groupage.notStored: This trip is not stored. It exists only on this screen; reloading clears it.
groupage.notAnExport: {{file}} is not a EMCargo shipment export and was skipped.
groupage.noDangerousGoods: {{file}} holds no dangerous goods and was skipped.
groupage.fromHistoryHint: The kept shipments you may see, with dangerous goods. Pick the ones on this vehicle; the same export the file route reads is used underneath.
groupage.searchHistory: Search by reference, consignor or consignee…
groupage.tripNamePlaceholder: Name of the trip: vehicle, route, date…
groupage.keepHint: This installation keeps its shipments; the assessed trip can be kept beside them. What is kept is what was on the vehicle, the permitted maximum mass and the judgement as it is given now, with the editions it was computed against.
groupage.kept: Trip kept. You will find it under Trips.
groupage.keepFailed: The trip could not be kept.

history.title: Shipments
history.intro: The shipments this installation kept. Open one in the wizard, download its documents again, or remove it.
history.off: This installation does not keep shipments. An administrator switches the history on under Settings, Administration, Keep shipments.
history.search: Search by reference, consignor or consignee…
history.empty: No shipments kept yet. The export step keeps one when its documents are downloaded, or when you press Keep in history.
history.documentsHint: The kept bundle, rendered again on today's build — the same code path as the export step's download.
history.documentsNone: Kept without ready documents, so there is nothing to render again. Open it in the wizard to finish it.
history.confirmRemove: Remove this shipment from the history? Documents that were downloaded are not affected.
history.keepHint: This installation keeps its shipments. Downloading the documents keeps this one as well; you can also keep it now.
history.loadFailed: This shipment could not be opened.
history.useTemplateHint: A new shipment with the same goods, parties and route; reference and dates left empty.
history.templateOpened: New shipment from {{reference}}: reference and dates are empty, the rest was taken over.

addressBook.title: Address book
addressBook.hint: Pick a party, or save what is here under its name.
addressBook.empty: Still empty — fill in a party and press Save.

articles.title: Articles
articles.intro: Your own article codes, linked to what the library knows about the substance and its packaging: UN number, proper shipping name, packing group, type of package and content per package. Entered once; on a goods line you pick the code and the dangerous goods step gets the rest. A spreadsheet goes in and out in the same columns.
articles.search: Search by code, name or UN number…
articles.empty: No articles yet. Add one or import a spreadsheet.

dgsa.title: DGSA annual report
dgsa.intro: The safety adviser's annual report (ADR 1.8.3.3): the figures over the kept shipments of one calendar year, and the adviser's duties as headings to fill in yourself. Download it as a workbook to keep — five years, the ADR says.
dgsa.unknownNote: {{count}} substance line(s) without a usable quantity or unit; they are not in the kilograms and litres.
dgsa.name: Proper shipping name
dgsa.adrPointsNote: As the application judged it when the shipment was kept: the 1.1.3.6 points count over the declared quantities.
dgsa.dutiesIntro: These are the points the ADR tells the adviser to check. The application does not fill them in — the judgement is the adviser's. The workbook has an empty column beside them.
dgsa.nothing: Nothing to report for this year.
dgsa.formIntro: The report in the shape of the DVSA template (the UK competent authority, December 2025). What the history can propose sits under a button; the answers are the adviser's and are kept per year.
dgsa.takeOverTable: Take over the classes and quantities from the history
dgsa.signatureSaved: Your saved signature from the settings is placed on the report.
dgsa.signatureMissing: No saved signature in your settings; the report gets a signature line.

departments.title: Departments
departments.intro: A department decides who sees whose kept shipments: a user sees their own department's, a user without one sees the unassigned, an administrator sees all. Without departments everybody sees everything.
departments.name: Department name
departments.confirmRemove: Remove {{name}}? Its users, shipments and trips keep existing; they just belong to no department any more.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.intro: Who did what, and when. Metadata only: the action, who, a short summary in the application's own words and the address the request came from. Never the contents of a shipment.
audit.retentionHint: The retention is set under Settings, Administration.

actions.user.two_factor_cleared: Two-factor verification of an account cleared
actions.shipment.documents: Documents of a kept shipment downloaded again
actions.shipment.export: Export of a kept shipment downloaded

trips.title: Trips
trips.intro: The groupage trips this installation kept: what was on the vehicle and the judgement as it was given at the time. Reopen one on the groupage page, or remove it.
trips.empty: No trips kept yet. The groupage page keeps a trip when you press Keep trip after the assessment.
trips.name: Name
trips.notFound: This trip does not exist, or you may not see it.
trips.confirmRemove: Remove this trip from the history? The kept shipments on it stay.
trips.keptAsJudged: The judgement below is as it was given when the trip was kept, under the editions the Editions line names. Reopening and assessing again gives today's judgement.

docgroups.intro: The questions are grouped by subject rather than by document. One answer counts for every document that asks for it. Fields marked * are required for export.

draft.kept: This entry is kept as a draft.
draft.failed: The draft could not be saved — your entry is still on the screen.
draft.resumed: Your earlier entry is back; you are where you left off.
draft.notKeptHere: This installation stores nothing: a reload loses your entry.
draft.notADraft: This file is not a EMCargo draft.

overview.title: Overview
overview.intro: Here is what needs your attention today
overview.introNoHistory: This installation keeps no shipments, so there is nothing to come back to. Starting one works here all the same.
overview.resumeTitle: Carry on where you left off
overview.search: Search recent shipments by reference or organisation
overview.loadError: Some information could not be loaded. Please try again.
overview.localStart: Start with your goods. Paste a list from Excel or choose a transport mode.

studio.importHint: Paste your goods list from Excel. EMCargo reads the rows and calculates weight and volume.
studio.loginHint: Sign in to continue with your shipments.
studio.historyPrivacy: With shipment history enabled, your drafts and saved shipments are stored on this installation.

settingsNav.intro: Personal preferences, organisation and system. All in one place.

updates.intro: Versions, progress and updates in one place.
updates.notChecked: Check whether a new version is available.
updates.unraid: Unraid: add the container variable UPDATE_APPLY_ENABLED with value true and map /var/run/docker.sock to the same container path. Apply the container. The update button then appears when a new release is available.

dgFocus.preparing: Updating substance details and follow-up questions…

dgFocus.chooseSubstance: Choose a substance first. Its details and questions will appear next.
